Clear. So the other person added `// hotfix applied directly` to `.gitignore` while you added `// local work`. Your version is tested and ready.

Since you're in a disposable environment and your version is the one that matters, the cleanest fix is to force-push your local main to origin/main, overwriting their hotfix:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin main
```

This keeps your tested version as the source of truth. The `--force-with-lease` is safer than `--force` because it will reject if someone else pushed in the meantime.

Want me to do this, or would you prefer a different approach (like rebasing their work on top of yours)?
